description: FIND-1003's fix (this round) correctly specifies the 2-argument `executeLoanIssuanceAttempt` call and correctly states `deps.getCitizen` must be a fresh, per-call closure. However, the closure's own specified RETURN SHAPE -- 'returns that SAME citizen record shape steps 1-5 already consume (`{id, wallet, walletAddress, coLocatedWithCoordinator, ...}`)' (behavioral-spec.md line 2606-2608) -- never mentions `balanceUsd`, and this omission is not cosmetic: the REAL, unmodified, already-converged (sprint-2) `runLockedIssuance` genuinely reads `freshBorrower.balanceUsd` (line 198, feeding `isBorrowerEligible`'s `borrowerBalanceUsd`) and `freshLender.balanceUsd` (line 214, feeding `computeLenderAvailableUsd`'s `lenderBalanceUsd`) directly off the citizen records `getCitizen` returns at step 6's fresh recheck. Both consumers fail CLOSED on a missing balance via `finiteOr` (`lending-gate.mjs:40-42`): `isBorrowerEligible` treats an undefined `borrowerBalanceUsd` as `Infinity` (`finiteOr(value, Infinity)`, line 110), which ALWAYS fails the `balance < BORROWER_LOW_USD` check (line 111) -- reason `not_broke_enough`; `computeLenderAvailableUsd` treats an undefined `lenderBalanceUsd` as `0` (line 54), driving `lenderAvailableUsd` to `0` and refusing at `decideLoan`. Empirically confirmed this review: live-executed the REAL, unmodified `executeLoanIssuanceAttempt` with a 2-argument call exactly matching REQ-117's own corrected step-6 shape -- `deps.getCitizen` returning EXACTLY the literal shape REQ-117's text specifies (`{id, wallet, walletAddress, coLocatedWithCoordinator}`, all other required-elsewhere fields present -- `fuel`/`humanDependencies` for `isSelfFunded`), deliberately WITHOUT a `balanceUsd` field (since REQ-117's own text never instructs the implementer to merge one in) -- against a fixture representing PROP-117c's own fixture-3 scenario (one broke citizen, one surplus citizen, both otherwise fully qualifying). Result: `{status:"refused", reason:"not_broke_enough"}` -- NOT a crash, but a SILENT, PERMANENT, systematically-wrong refusal of the exact scenario this REQ exists to make reachable, for every real wake, regardless of the citizens' real balances. This is the SAME severity class of defect FIND-1003 fixed (REQ-117's own EARS clause -- 'genuinely INVOKED... when a real eligible candidate exists' -- is violated), except the failure mode is silent business-logic-shaped refusal rather than an uncaught exception, making it HARDER to detect in production (no crash, no error log, no exit-code-1 daemon-failure signal -- exit `0`, indistinguishable from an ordinary, legitimate 'no eligible pair' wake per this REQ's own step-9 exit-code discipline). Critically, PROP-117c's own fixture-3 verification-method text (verification-architecture.md line 192) is TOO PERMISSIVE to catch this: it asserts the call 'genuinely RETURNS a `{status:"active"|"disbursement_failed"|"disbursement_uncertain"|"refused"}` value rather than throwing' -- `"refused"` is explicitly one of the four accepted outcomes, so a test built exactly to this literal spec text, run against a naive-but-textually-faithful implementation of the getCitizen closure (omitting balanceUsd, exactly as REQ-117's own shape enumeration invites), would report a PASS while the underlying wiring remains genuinely, completely broken for its own named scenario ('one broke, one with surplus' never actually reaches `active`). Root cause: REQ-117's step-4 text frames balance-fetching as an action performed FOR candidate citizens during wake-gate.mjs's OWN discovery loop, never explicitly stating that the SAME freshly-fetched balance must also be MERGED into the citizen record object `getCitizen` returns for `executeLoanIssuanceAttempt`'s own separate, later fresh recheck.

evidence.snippet: THE SYSTEM SHALL supply `deps.getCitizen` as a real, production `async (id) => {...}` closure that performs a FRESH read of the citizens registry ... and returns that SAME citizen record shape steps 1-5 already consume (`{id, wallet, walletAddress, coLocatedWithCoordinator, ...}`), or `null` for an unknown id.
asserts the call genuinely RETURNS a `{status:"active"|"disbursement_failed"|"disbursement_uncertain"|"refused"}` value rather than throwing

evidence.location: fresh execution this review, `node` against the real, unmodified lending-orchestrator.mjs/lending-gate.mjs, deps.getCitizen returning REQ-117's own literally-specified shape with no balanceUsd merged in
evidence.description: `await executeLoanIssuanceAttempt({lenderId:'lenderA', borrowerId:'borrowerB', nowMs}, {getCitizen, gojoLogRows:[], ledgerFile, lockStatePath, disburse: stub})` (correct 2-argument call, no crash) returned `{"status":"refused","reason":"not_broke_enough"}` for a fixture representing two fully-qualifying citizens (self-funded, EVM-walleted, co-located, one genuinely broke, one with surplus) -- proving the getCitizen closure shape REQ-117's own text specifies produces a permanent false refusal, not the `active` outcome PROP-117c's fixture-3 is named for. A SEPARATE control run, identical except `getCitizen` also merges a real `balanceUsd` onto each returned citizen record (an addition NOT instructed anywhere in REQ-117's own text), returned `{"status":"active","loanId":"loan_lenderA_1"}` -- confirming `balanceUsd` is the ONLY missing ingredient and that its omission, not any other defect, is the root cause.

recommendation: Amend REQ-117's step-6 `getCitizen` contract to explicitly state that the returned citizen record SHALL include a `balanceUsd` field carrying a FRESH USDC balance fetched via the SAME `_shared/lib/usdc.mjs::usdcBalance(citizen.walletAddress.evm, {fetchImpl})` primitive step 4 already uses (reusing step 4's own `fetchImpl` override seam for this second, later fetch too -- never a stale copy of step 4's own already-gathered candidate-selection balance, mirroring this REQ's own 'never a pre-lock snapshot' discipline already applied to registry freshness). Explicitly list `balanceUsd` alongside `id`/`wallet`/`walletAddress`/`coLocatedWithCoordinator` in the closure's stated return shape (remove the vague trailing `...`). Tighten PROP-117c's own fixture-3 assertion so it cannot be satisfied by a `"refused"` outcome for this specific fixture -- since fixture 3 is deliberately constructed with one broke and one surplus, otherwise-fully-qualifying citizen, the ONLY behaviorally-correct outcome is `status==="active"` (or, if the stub `disburse` is made to fail, `"disbursement_failed"`/`"disbursement_uncertain"` -- but never `"refused"`, since nothing about this fixture's own construction should trigger a REQ-101/102/106/112 refusal reason); a `"refused"` result for fixture 3 specifically should FAIL the test, not pass it.
